## The emulator was lying, and every visual decision was made against it

Sixteen commits, and the one that matters most changed no firmware at all.

This project decides geometry by measuring rendered frames. Squachy's scale, the pet's perch, the bubble headroom, the counter rows — all settled by looking at emulator output. That makes `sim/TFT_eSPI.h` a measuring instrument rather than a convenience, and an instrument that disagrees with the hardware is worse than none, because it gives confident wrong answers.

It disagreed in four places.

**The font cell was seven rows.** The real one is eight — `fontdata[1].height` is 8, and `drawChar` opens `setWindow(x, y, x+5, y+7)`. Two consequences, and the second is the expensive one. Row eight is where descenders live, so the emulator clipped them off every lowercase word. And `fontHeight()` feeds row arithmetic: on the LOG screen a row came to 24 pixels in the emulator against the device's 27, so it drew **eight rows of detections where the hardware draws seven**, with text overlapping in a way real glass never shows.

**Round-rect corners swept a full 360 degrees.** `drawCircleQuadrants` did this despite its name, its comment, and an unnamed trailing bool plainly meant to select the quadrant and never read. So `drawRoundRect` stamped four complete circles inset from the corners, and since every caller fills then outlines, three quarters of each landed on top of the fill. Measured on a 160×80 rect with r=20: 352 outline pixels inside the shape, now zero. The toasters and all four speech bubbles wore them.

**Every character was a column short.** The real `drawChar` paints six columns; the sixth is always blank and exists to be filled with the background. The shim painted five, so opaque text — an unbroken box on hardware — showed a one-pixel bar of whatever was underneath between every pair of characters. Underneath, on this project, is a sunset. Exactly the sort of artefact somebody then "fixes" in the firmware.

**Ellipses accepted radii the hardware rejects.** The real library opens `fillEllipse` with `if (rx<2) return; if (ry<2) return;`. The shim drew a stripe instead, so a scaled-down sprite could show detail the hardware never renders.

### What actually moved

Measured by rendering seven screens before and after: **settings 39% of pixels, log 31%, detection filter 22%**, alert 5%, boot 0.2%, diary 0.02%, clear 1.1%. The text-heavy screens, as expected.

And the reassuring half: on CLEAR only rows 189–209 changed — the counter text. Everything above is pixel-identical, so Squachy's scale, his footing and the per-outfit overflow guard were all measured against frames that were right. `ui_clear`'s `lineH` is a hard-coded 14 rather than derived from `fontHeight`, which is what spared it.

A separate emulator bug had been hiding just as much. The ALERT screen called `engine.logAt(0)` — whatever `seedDetections` wrote last, which has been the drone since the drone was added. **Every alert frame anyone had ever rendered was a DRONE**, and the other sixteen types' headlines, colours and confidence rows had never once been looked at on a desktop. `--alert N` fixes that, and errors out with a pointer to `seedDetections()` rather than silently falling back.

An eighth test suite pins all of it, with every value read out of the vendored TFT_eSPI source rather than from what looked right. It asks the font table which character has ink on the bottom row instead of assuming one.

## HACKER

Type 17: Flipper Zero, Pwnagotchi, WiFi Pineapple and the ESP deauther family in one bucket. Four products under one type because what matters to somebody reading the screen is that a tool for attacking radios is in the room, not which model — the model goes in the vendor label, and where the device announces a name, that name goes in the log row.

Filed red with DEAUTH and EVILTWIN rather than cyan with the cameras. Everything else here is equipment that watches; this is equipment that transmits at other radios.

**Flipper Zero**, four signatures, three exact: service UUIDs `0x3081`/`82`/`83` (one per case colour), SIG company ID `0x0E29`, IEEE OUI `0C:FA:22`, and an advertised name beginning "Flipper" — that last graded down, because the owner can type anything there.

**Two constants the ecosystem has wrong, and neither is shipped here.** Marauder's source comments Flipper's company ID as `0x0FBA`; `0x0FBA` is Cosonic Intelligent Technologies, who make headsets, and every project that copied that constant inherited it. Wall-of-Flippers checks `80:E1:26` and `80:E1:27`; neither is in the IEEE registry under Flipper or anybody. Same failure as `00:0E:58`, which sat here for eleven releases labelled "Vigilant" while belonging to Sonos. A test pins both, so a re-import from another detector turns it red.

**Pwnagotchi is the strongest signature on the device, because it volunteers.** They find each other by putting a plain-ASCII JSON blob in a vendor element of their own beacons — name, version, uptime, handshake count, deauth policy. There is no JSON parser: that would cost heap and time on every beacon in the air. Two byte scans instead. `pwnd_tot` is what makes it a pwnagotchi rather than any other device with a brace in its beacon, and the name is what the log shows. That name is attacker-controlled and lands in a rendered field, so anything outside printable ASCII is rejected.

**Pineapple and deauthers are circumstantial, and graded that way**: SSID prefixes `Pineapple_` and `pwned` at Medium, Hak5's `02:C0:CA` and `02:13:37` at Low. Hak5 hold no IEEE registration at all — forty thousand rows, no entry — because their gear is OpenWRT on ODM boards. Those two addresses are a real habit and a real hint, but both are locally administered, so by construction they identify nobody.

**Not in this bucket: bare Espressif.** A nyanBOX, a Marauder, an M5Stack and a SquachWatch are the same chip, and sixteen Espressif prefixes already sit under FLOCK. Two types fighting over one prefix would have every SquachWatch flag every other one.

On the counter row, **HACK takes EVIL's column** and EVILTWIN's count folds into it. A rogue AP is not a category of hardware, it is a thing this hardware does, and a Pineapple running PineAP karma *is* an evil twin — the same box seen by behaviour instead of signature. DEAUTH keeps its own column for the reverse reason: plenty of things that are not a Pineapple produce a burst.

**Device names in the log.** `Detection` has carried `name[20]` all along and nothing ever drew it, so a Flipper's name, a Pwnagotchi's name, an iBeacon's deployment and a drone's serial were all captured and then thrown away at the last step.

## The alert screen, rebuilt

The old layout put eight rows of near-equal weight on one screen and let a sunset run behind six-pixel text.

**A header strip in the detection's own colour.** Three things fall out of that: the category reads before any word does — attack types red, cameras cyan, trackers purple; the pulsing border's six pixels come back on all four sides; and `!! DETECTION !!` is gone, because the whole screen is the detection and that row was spending the best real estate restating it. The type name is set in Bangers, measured against the space actually left beside the IGNORE button rather than against the screen width — which is the sort of thing that only shows up on the narrow board.

**IGNORE is a real Windows 95 push button.** Silver face, two-pixel bevel, black system-font label, centred in the strip. MUTED is the same button *held down* rather than a differently coloured one — Win95 had an idiom for a button that stays in after you let go, and it fits exactly, so the state costs no new colour, no legend and nothing to learn.

Its five greys are deliberately not the authentic hex values. Written first as the real ones, the bevel came out lavender with its inner lit ring missing entirely: **the panel does not round 565 down to RGB332, it truncates**, and `#c0c0c0` and `#dfdfdf` both land on the same level — which, with only four blue levels available, is a pale lilac rather than any grey at all. The ramp is now built from levels the framebuffer can actually reach.

**One gauge instead of two objects.** The old screen had a small radar tucked under the readout *and* a separate icon at the bottom of the panel, and the two never met: one said a contact is out there, the other said this is what it is. The gauge went from r=38 to r=60 and the icon moved inside it with the instrument grid over the top.

Deliberately **not** viewer-centred with the icon on a bearing. The bearing is derived from the MAC, so it holds still during an alert and is otherwise arbitrary — one antenna cannot do direction finding, and putting a recognisable object at a compass position would claim it can. Distance is honest, so the rings carry that and the object sits at the centre.

## Every icon redrawn

`drawAlertFx` is gone, replaced by `drawTypeIcon`. The old one anchored its art at a fixed position and repainted the whole panel, which was fine while the icon was scenery and useless the moment it had to sit inside a gauge.

The art behind it was worse than "could be nicer". **Seventeen real detection types shared seven drawings, and four drew nothing at all.** One camera glyph served FLOCK, AXON, ALPR, CAMERA and RING — an ALPR camera and a police body camera were pixel-identical — and one purple pebble served all three trackers. DEAUTH, EVILTWIN, IBEACON and HACKER fired alerts over an empty field.

Every type now has its own object, and two shared helpers keep them a family: `housing()` lights every box from the same direction, and `lens()` — dark socket, glass, catchlight — is used by all five cameras and the drone's gimbal, so they read as related products while staying individually tellable.

The rule that took four passes to learn, written down because it is not obvious: **nothing is drawn in a value close to the ground.** BG is (10,0,15), so anything below roughly (70,70,80) disappears into it. Sunglasses, a raven and a camera dome all came out as holes the first time, because the subject being black had been taken to mean the drawing is. A black object at forty pixels is a mid tone with dark accents and a lit edge.

## The main screen says less

**ALL CLEAR is gone**, and so is the label that replaced it. It was a second headline state to keep in sync, and the counters answer it better — a screen of zeroes *is* all clear. Then the remaining label sat there reading ACTIVE DETECTIONS over those zeroes, which is simply untrue, since the device is idle far more than it is detecting.

The headline only draws when something is live now. Not lifetime: a camera seen an hour ago is not something happening, and the counters decay for the same reason. Its arrival is the event, so the glitch fires on the *edge* — once, when the screen goes from nothing to something, not again when a second detection joins the first.

Blank turned out to be the better screen rather than a compromise. Squachy's geometry hangs off the counter block, not that row, so he does not move — he is simply no longer painted over by a headline whose twenty-four-pass black outline exists specifically to be legible on top of him. The pet and the Mowin' Man stop running in behind it too.

When something *is* there, the row now says **NEARBY**, in the larger Bangers face. One word because the subject was the vague half, and the size is a consequence of the word: the old seventeen-character headline needed the smaller face just to fit, where this uses under a third of a landscape row.

**The reassurance moved to Squachy**, on a fixed thirty-second beat with ten lines. Checked ahead of the random idle roll, because that roll re-arms anywhere from nine to thirty-two seconds out and a dependable beat cannot be one of its outcomes. Skipped rather than queued while he is onboarding, showing off, asleep or already talking — a scripted line landing on top of a nap reads as a bug.

## Also

**Squachy defaults to MEDIUM.** Only consulted on a board that has never been told otherwise; anyone who has touched SIZE has a stored value.

**A walk-cycle fix, reported as VOID EYE's legs detaching.** Not the outfit and not the size: the leg's top moved down while the torso stayed put, so on half the cycle the leg came away from the hip. The overlap is about two pixels at any scale and the swing opens a five-or-six pixel hole, which is why it looked outfit-specific. The hip is pinned now and the leg changes length instead, which is also what a leg does.

**The rotation button hides when rotation is locked**, and on the AWOK board, where it never did anything.

**The owl's speech bubble sizes itself like every other bubble.** It was a hard-coded height where Squachy's and the pet's both derive from `fontHeight()`, which left the text one pixel of clearance and nowhere for a descender — and made it read as smaller than his, when both have always been the same size.

**Two hand-cut Bangers glyphs**, `-` and `'`. The renderer skips an unknown glyph with no advance, so a missing apostrophe would have silently rendered a contraction as a plural. Both are authored from the existing `!` stem rather than invented, so they inherit the real brush width and lean.

**MORE INFO and the README brought back in line with the firmware.** Five panels had drifted. UNKNOWN claimed "this matched a known fingerprint" when it is in fact the clamp target for an out-of-range type — reached when *nothing* matched, the exact opposite. FLOCK never mentioned the audit, which is the most useful thing anyone can know about that type. RAVEN implied ShotSpotter coverage this device does not have and cannot have. IBEACON never said it ships switched off.

### The actually-useful part

- **Added**: `HACKER` detection — Flipper Zero, Pwnagotchi, WiFi Pineapple and ESP deauthers
- **Added**: device names in the log, for anything that broadcasts one
- **Added**: a distinct icon for all eighteen detection types, where seven drawings had covered seventeen and four drew nothing
- **Added**: a Windows 95 IGNORE button on the alert screen, with MUTED as the same button held down
- **Added**: Squachy says he is watching every thirty seconds, from ten lines
- **Added**: `--alert N` in the emulator, and three more host test suites (eight total)
- **Changed**: the alert screen is built around a coloured header strip, with the detection's icon inside one large gauge
- **Changed**: the main screen's headline is blank while nothing is live, and glitches in as `NEARBY` when something is
- **Changed**: `HACK` takes `EVIL`'s counter column and absorbs its count
- **Changed**: Squachy defaults to MEDIUM
- **Changed**: `PENTEST HARDWARE` reads `HACKER HARDWARE`
- **Fixed**: the emulator drew an eight-row log where the hardware draws seven, clipped every descender, ringed every speech bubble and toaster with stray pixels, and showed a one-pixel gap between characters that hardware never has
- **Fixed**: every alert frame the emulator had ever rendered was a drone, whatever type was asked for
- **Fixed**: Squachy's legs detached from his hips during the walk cycle, at every size
- **Fixed**: the alert gauge overlapped the header strip, and was centred on the wrong band
- **Fixed**: the owl's speech bubble was too short for the font it holds
- **Fixed**: the rotation button showed on boards and modes where it does nothing
- **Fixed**: five MORE INFO panels described the firmware as it used to be, including UNKNOWN, which said the exact opposite of what it means
